summary: Deferred pin commitment causes split-cohort responses during canary cutover
description: Issue summary: During a planned canary rollout of gptx-13b-redwood-v1 for AcmePayments (enterprise), some user sessions were routed to the canary while others observed the pinned model version. Impact: inconsistent responses for the same prompt across simultaneous user sessions (observed in 12 distinct request traces), causing incorrect transaction descriptions in customer QA. Environment: prod-us-east (hosted API, dedicated route pinned by AcmePayments).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer created a route with a pinned model version (gptx-13b-redwood-v1) for their /generate endpoint.
2) Redwood performed a canary rollout to add a quantized variant (gptx-13b-q4) with 10% weight in us-east around 2026-03-12T17:05:00Z.
3) Multiple simultaneous requests from the same customer session were sent before pin commit finished; some were answered by pinned variant, others by the canary.
4) Compare outputs for identical prompts; observe variance in phrasing and tokenization that affected downstream QA checks.

trace_id=trc_0a9f3e; timestamp=2026-03-12T17:05:12Z; route=acmepayments/txn-gen; backend=pool-3; model=gptx-13b-redwood-v1; decision=pinned
edge-proxy logs show pin-commit event queued at 2026-03-12T17:04:59Z and confirmation delivered to routers at 2026-03-12T17:06:01Z
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: routing cache TTL + deferred pin commit transaction allowing routing decisions to consult stale policy leading to split-cohort.
Checked console: pin create API returned 200 at 2026-03-12T17:04:58Z but commit coordinator log shows a deferred commit due to in-flight canary weight adjustment job.
Router logs show per-connection decision made from local cache when commit was still pending; subsequently the commit propagated and future connections consistently used pinned model.
No GPU OOMs or autoscaler evictions recorded in implicated pools during window (monitoring graphs attached to PR).
Related change: autoscaler scheduling job PR #2148 attempted a transient capacity shift that touched the canary allocation during commit window — likely exacerbated timing race.
Confirmed at least 12 customer request traces where different model ids are returned for identical session and prompt (sampled traces included above).
Customer side: AcmePayments reported downstream QA failures affecting nightly reconciliation; they provided example prompts and timestamps.
resolution: Mitigation applied 2026-03-12T18:00Z: forced pin-commit sweep issued (admin override) which reconciled router caches and set pin_state=committed across us-east routers.
Rollout paused for AcmePayments and canary weight rolled back to 0% until a safe commit path is implemented.

Hotfix deployed 2026-03-13T02:15Z: add gating in commit coordinator so pin commit cannot be marked 'queued/deferred' while concurrent canary-weight jobs are active; PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2154.
Follow-ups: add end-to-end test covering concurrent commit+canary update, increase routing cache TTL observability, and update runbook to include admin sweep command used in mitigation.
Customer communication: sent remediation note and workaround (pause canary) and scheduled postmortem with AcmePayments for 2026-03-15.
Status: workaround in place, long-term fix merged; monitoring alert created to detect 'deferred_commit' state during rollouts.
